sources.note: equipment plan source (research grade: datasheet); size 237 x 243 x 351 mm (w x d x h); port and control positions are placeholders until measured

Genelec 8341A product page (downloaded and read): analog input "XLR female, balanced 10 kOhm", AES/EBU "Digital signal input connector XLR female 110 Ohm", AES/EBU "output / Thru connector XLR male 110 Ohm", "Two CAT5 (RJ45) GLM Network connectors", mains "100-240 VAC 50/60Hz" (the inlet type is not named: iec-c14 follows the Genelec 8030C and the KH 120 II precedents), dimensions "Height 351 mm, Width 237 mm, Depth 243 mm" without Iso-Pod (370 mm with), driver sizes bass racetrack 2 x 170 x 90 mm, coaxial midrange 90 mm and 19 mm metal dome. Documents the connector set (portsDocumented): analog XLR in, AES/EBU in and thru, two GLM network ports, mains inlet. The GLM ports carry control data, not audio: they keep the catalogue signal aoip, as the KH 120 II RJ45 does.

build params: the shipped Genelec 8030C recipe (curved-cabinet: a rounded polygon plan, elliptic fillets, a shallow barrel arc) scaled to 237 x 243 x 351, plus a 104 mm coaxial waveguide dish around the 60 mm coax recess at 262 mm. The two racetrack bass drivers (170 x 90 mm) are not round, so they are drawn on the baffle picture only (their position is a guess); the real unit and its Iso-Pod stand are not modelled (the plan size excludes the Iso-Pod). The recess positions and the barrel are estimates from the datasheet outline, not measured. Port and control positions on the rear: no drawing or photo was opened, so every position is a plausible guess (confidence guess).

build.projection io + opposite: our own generic artwork (content/generic-panels/<id>.json, drawn by npm run asset:panel): the rear panel with sockets drawn at the port positions and the baffle with drivers drawn at the datasheet sizes; no photo copy, no brand mark, no lettering. Colour: a studio-monitor default (the page lists white, dark grey, black and raw finishes), lifted for the creation lighting.
